focus: Point photometry: inverse-square and cosine units, incidence direction, finite/nonnegative output, zero and invalid inputs. Scene schema validation and rectangular integration excluded.

checks.outcome: Read mandatory startup documents remotely. Existing thresholds and requirement for actual Debug/Release evidence retained.

checks.check: Normal-incidence units and supported scene range
checks.outcome: Source-derived: candela divided by squared meter distance gives lux; valid intensity range is 0...100000 cd; finite distance >=0.05 m. Within bounded scene positions distance is <=sqrt(120000) m and accepted normal illuminance remains finite and nonnegative.

Source-derived: delta=source-receiver points toward incident light; normalized dot with receiver normal clamped to [0,1] gives projected incidence. Zero intensity and back-facing normal yield zero for otherwise supported geometry; coincident or <5cm separation returns nil before division by distance.

Source-derived: nonfinite/negative/out-of-range candela and nonfinite/too-short distances return nil; invalid source/receiver positions return nil. UnitDirection rejects zero/nonfinite vectors and scales components before normalization to avoid finite-component overflow.

Inspected SurfacePhotometryTests.testPointCosineAndInverseSquare: 400 cd at 2m is compared with 100*cos(theta) lux at 0/30/60/90/120/180 degrees with backward cosine clamped; 1m case expects 400 lux. Coincident source and negative infinity intensity assert nil. testDirectionNormalizesAndRejectsInvalid covers 3-4-5 direction, greatest-finite inputs, zero, NaN and infinity. Tests were not executed.

PhotometryInvariantTests independently builds proper rotations and translations and compares point lux for three surface normals across four transforms at relative/absolute 1e-9 tolerance. Mixed-rig yaw/translation test preserves meter and study outputs; rectangle/BRDF implementations were outside this review.
PrototypeTests covers valid recipe round trips and persistence; its invalid-light edit test asserts saved data preservation, not direct point-photometry output. No runtime inference made.
Found one source-derived arithmetic overflow corner detailed below.

findings.title: Standalone normalIlluminance loses representable positive output when accepted distance squared overflows
findings.repro: Call Photometry.normalIlluminance(candela: 100000, distanceMeters: 1e155). The inputs satisfy the function guards. IEEE-754 Double multiplication distanceMeters * distanceMeters overflows to infinity, so the implementation returns 0 instead of the representable mathematical result approximately 1e-305 lux.
findings.impact: Low priority: affects the public standalone helper's accepted unbounded finite distance range. Scene-based pointIlluminance validates Position coordinates in -100...100 m, so ordinary app scene calculations cannot reach this case.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute (candela / distanceMeters) / distanceMeters, or explicitly enforce/document a bounded standalone distance domain; preserve existing normal scene results. Add a focused extreme finite-distance regression if changing the helper.
